rows.message: In the Saffire-II strip with Nomex attached to acrylic, which component actually burned?
rows.reference_answer: The upstream PMMA/acrylic burned. No Nomex ignition was observed.

response.answer:
An upstream 5 cm PMMA strip overlapped Nomex HT90-40. At about 22.1% oxygen and 20 cm/s concurrent flow in orbital microgravity, PMMA was consumed. The first centimetre of Nomex was damaged and the first five were blackened. Table I records zero Nomex burn length. [1]

2. Saffire-II, what ignited at a material interface. Sample 2-7 used a 5-cm PMMA lead-in and 24-cm length of Nomex HT90-40 with about 7 mm overlap. The PSI table lists approximately 22.1% oxygen, 20 cm/s concurrent flow, 80 W igniter power, 9.2 s igniter time and 140 s composite burn duration. Its phase-specific result is 5 cm PMMA consumed and zero Nomex burn length. NASA also describes significant damage to the first centimetre and blackening over the first five. Soot deposition is one possible explanation for discoloration. The assembly’s elapsed time cannot serve as either a Nomex ignition delay or a Nomex burn duration. Ground experiments with the same grade found that PMMA could support Nomex burning in ambient air until the external flame burned out. Rank support for the exact composite event separately from support for assisted or self-sustained Nomex spread in a changed atmosphere. [2]

rows.message: Which two smoke-producing materials caused many missed ISS alarms in SAME?
rows.reference_answer: Kapton and Teflon smoke.

response.answer:
Meyer et al. compared signals from two detector technologies against alarm thresholds in SAME. The ISS light-scattering detector would have missed over half of the Kapton smoke tests and two-thirds of the Teflon tests. It responded strongly to several larger-particle smokes. [1]

4. SAME, measured smoke and the likelihood of an alarm. In §3.2 of their original study, Meyer and colleagues compare sensor responses against a dashed alarm threshold in Figure 9. The ISS light-scattering unit would have missed over half the tested Kapton cases and two-thirds of the Teflon cases. The same detector produced large responses to several other smokes. The Shuttle detector had fewer usable observations. Preserve each fraction exactly at the authors’ level of reporting: there is no basis here for a per-material denominator extrapolated from the total number of runs. In the PSI reflight table, runs 51 and 101 both list 60 s at the source but differ in inlet flow, heater setting and net aging. Their 60 s is a generation setting. The experiment does not supply a time-to-alarm for a lunar cabin. [2]

rows.reference_answer: The burner stream carried it into the chamber.

Only A2 recorded hot ignition, for two seconds before self-extinction. The original PSI table records approximate pressure of 2.2066 bar in both rows, while Appendix E of the dissertation reports nominal 2.0 atm. Direct conversion of 2.0 atm yields 2.0265 bar: the two values are different reported quantities. Keep the original field and qualifier with each value. rows.message: How many burns were planned in the 2026 FM² design?
rows.reference_answer: Four separate burns.

response.answer:
The April 2026 NASA FY 2027 budget request describes planned lunar FM² work in 2027. This review has no verified launch date or actual flight outcome. A budget year does not establish a launch commitment. [1]

7. FM², prediction with four dependent trials. The March 2026 design supersedes a 2024 configuration involving two different fuels. On viewer p. 10 it specifies Synergy Pro Navy; the older shortlist table on viewer p. 14 calls one candidate Natural Synergy Pro. Confirm grade, finish and lot before joining a comparison. With a nominally common limiting oxygen concentration for the four specimens, outcomes are dependent and the effective sample size is small. A Brier score can compare predictions on resolved indices. It cannot establish calibration from one four-burn mission. NASA gives qualitative expectations and a 24–26% expected LOC. The guide's 26%/1.5 percentage-point distribution is a teaching assumption. A shared oxygen threshold assumes that sufficient starting oxygen will produce sustained spread after a functioning igniter. Registering a separate ignition model would be necessary to estimate a distinct ignition-failure probability. A nominal attempt with no ignition and an invalid igniter have different scoring dispositions. A changed design or missing footage can also make an observation unscorable. The April FY 2027 budget request plans FM² lunar work for 2027. These documents provide the design and planning basis; an official result with traceable per-burn outcomes is still needed for scoring. [2]

rows.message: Was it the visibly blackened part that burned?

history.content: Which trial placed acrylic beside Nomex?

rows.reference_answer: The PMMA strip burned. Nomex blackened without observed ignition.

response.answer:
An upstream 5 cm PMMA strip overlapped Nomex HT90-40. At about 22.1% oxygen and 20 cm/s concurrent flow in orbital microgravity, PMMA was consumed. The first centimetre of Nomex was damaged and the first five were blackened. Table I records zero Nomex burn length. [1]

2. Saffire-II, what ignited at a material interface. Sample 2-7 used a 5-cm PMMA lead-in and 24-cm length of Nomex HT90-40 with about 7 mm overlap. The PSI table lists approximately 22.1% oxygen, 20 cm/s concurrent flow, 80 W igniter power, 9.2 s igniter time and 140 s composite burn duration. Its phase-specific result is 5 cm PMMA consumed and zero Nomex burn length. NASA also describes significant damage to the first centimetre and blackening over the first five. Soot deposition is one possible explanation for discoloration. The assembly’s elapsed time cannot serve as either a Nomex ignition delay or a Nomex burn duration. Ground experiments with the same grade found that PMMA could support Nomex burning in ambient air until the external flame burned out. Rank support for the exact composite event separately from support for assisted or self-sustained Nomex spread in a changed atmosphere. [2]

7. FM², prediction with four dependent trials. The March 2026 design supersedes a 2024 configuration involving two different fuels. On viewer p. 10 it specifies Synergy Pro Navy; the older shortlist table on viewer p. 14 calls one candidate Natural Synergy Pro. Confirm grade, finish and lot before joining a comparison. With a nominally common limiting oxygen concentration for the four specimens, outcomes are dependent and the effective sample size is small. A Brier score can compare predictions on resolved indices. A shared oxygen threshold assumes that sufficient starting oxygen will produce sustained spread after a functioning igniter. Registering a separate ignition model would be necessary to estimate a distinct ignition-failure probability. A nominal attempt with no ignition and an invalid igniter have different scoring dispositions. A changed design or missing footage can also make an observation unscorable. The April FY 2027 budget request plans FM² lunar work for 2027. These documents provide the design and planning basis; an official result with traceable per-burn outcomes is still needed for scoring.
